question.prompt:
Mr. Zhou places all the integers from \(1\) to \(225\) into a \(15\) by \(15\) grid. He places \(1\) in the middle square (eighth row and eighth column) and places other numbers one by one clockwise, as shown in part in the diagram below. What is the sum of the greatest number and the least number that appear in the second row from the top?

[Figure 1](figures/2021_AMC_10B_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The diagram shows that each square layer finishes across its top edge from left to right. After reaching the upper-right corner, the spiral moves one square right and traces the next border down, left, up, and finally right. Thus every completed centered \(n\times n\) square, for odd \(n\), ends with \(n^2\) in its upper-right corner: its \(n^2\) cells contain the integers from \(1\) through \(n^2\).

The centered \(13\times13\) square occupies rows \(2\) through \(14\) and columns \(2\) through \(14\) of the full grid. Its top row ends at \(13^2=169\). There are \(12\) steps from its leftmost cell to its rightmost cell, so that row runs from
\[
169-12=157\quad\text{through}\quad169.
\]
Only the two end cells of the requested row remain. Immediately after \(169\), the spiral moves right, placing \(170\) in column \(15\) of row \(2\). The completed outer square ends with \(15^2=225\) at its upper-right corner. Moving \(14\) cells left along its top row reaches \(225-14=211\); the cell directly below that is \(210\).

We have therefore accounted for all \(15\) cells of the second row:
\[
210,\ 157,\ 158,\ldots,\ 169,\ 170.
\]
The least entry is \(157\), and the greatest is \(210\). Their sum is \(\boxed{367}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Track completed square layers
